terms._about: Words a theme may rename everywhere at once. Use {{mon}} in any string. {{rival}} and {{Rival}} become the opponent's character name during a game; these are the words used when they have none.

_about: Every word in the game. To translate: copy this file (e.g. ja.json), translate the values, keep the keys and the {placeholders}, and add it to config.json. Entries with one/other are plurals; add the forms your language needs (zero, two, few, many). Inline <b> is allowed.

ingredients._about: One list per element, in order of how far the ingredient moves (1, 2, 3 squares). The pairs (AF air and fire, AW, FE, EW) move diagonally, 1 then 2 squares.

rules.title: How to play

goal.p: Rival apothecaries race to {end} {{mon}}. Every patient is a small map: cure them by playing ingredient cards that move your marker from the start ◯ to the cure {cure}.

turn.p: Do one action: Gather {gather} market cards (or draw {gather} blind), or Brew a cure. Once each per turn, before or after, you may also plant a hand card in your garden and buy a tool.

brew.p: Pick a patient (tap it, or swipe the map), then tap a card to preview its move. Play it, or cancel and try another. Tap a numbered chip to go back to that card. Each element moves in a straight line its own way: {dirs}, exactly as many squares as its card shows. A card with two elements moves diagonally between their ways. A Kitsune Tail {kitsune} moves one square any way, diagonals too. Straight moves can't pass through an oni {oniG}; diagonals slip past. Nothing may land on an oni or leave the map. Finish exactly on {cure}, using at least {min} hand card. Hand cards are spent; garden cards stay.

fame.p: A cured patient is worth its number in {{mon}}. Passing a sakura {sakura} adds {sak}.

tools.p: One of each in a two-player game, paid for with {{mon}} (your marker moves back). Each works once per brew.

curse.p: Once per turn, after your action, you may lay one of your {oni} oni on a patient to claim them. Your rival can't cure a patient you've claimed. Cure them on your next turn and you get {sak} extra {{mon}}, like a sakura. If your next turn ends and they're still uncured, the oni goes and your rival gets the {sak} {{mon}} instead.

end.p: Garden holds {garden}; planting into a full garden discards one. Hand limit {hand} at the end of your turn. When someone reaches {end}, the round finishes so both play equally; it also ends after the village runs out. Most {{mon}} wins; ties go to most cures.

patients.p: Every patient has an element (the badge on their portrait). Once cured they join your ward, and each ward patient helps you once: in any brew it can leap 2 squares one way and 1 to the side, over anything between, or be used as a known cure.

rules.needEl: A cure needs at least one ingredient of the patient's element (the big sign in a card's corner). The Kitsune Tail {kitsune} counts as any element. A two-element card counts as either.

known.p: If an unused ward patient had the same ailment, you can cure the new patient without ingredients for half its value (at least 1). That uses up the ward patient.

guild.p: Your guild has an element. Once per brew you may play one garden card of that element twice, so plant those.

bench.p: Patients wait on a bench of four spots. Fresh arrivals need only {b3} ingredients; the longer they wait, the more a cure takes and the more it pays, up to {b0} ingredients and +{x0} on last chance. When someone is cured, the others move up. At the end of each round the last-chance patient goes home uncured.

symptoms.p: Harder patients show symptom marks on their map. The route must pass through every one before it ends on the cure. Straight moves pass through squares; diagonal moves and leaps only count where they land.

quirks.p: Some patients have a quirk: frail (no diagonals or leaps), nervous (hand cards only), stubborn (two of their element) or contagious (if they go home uncured, both lose {cont}). Some give a gift when cured: {{mon}}, a card for your garden, an oni back, cards from the deck, or a cheaper tool. Every cured patient still joins your ward.

royal.p: Each healer has a private royal patient with {stages} stages. Cure them in order, each with at least {rmin} ingredients, as your turn's action. A royal pays {rpay} {{mon}}, but only once every stage is done, and doesn't join your ward.

install.title: Install Kusurifuda
install.sub: Gets its own icon, opens full screen, and plays offline.
install.done: Installed. Open it from your home screen or app list.

steps: Tap Share {share} (bottom bar on iPhone, top bar on iPad).
Scroll down and tap Add to Home Screen, then Add.
ios.note: Chrome and Edge on iOS 16.4 or later have the same Share › Add to Home Screen.

steps: Tap Install if your browser offers it.
Otherwise open the browser menu {menu} and choose Install app or Add to Home screen.
android.note: Works in Chrome, Edge, Samsung Internet and Firefox.

steps: In the menu bar choose File › Add to Dock.
Click the install icon at the right end of the address bar.
Or open the browser menu and choose Install Kusurifuda (in Chrome it sits under Cast, save and share).
desktop.note: It opens in its own window and shows up with your other apps.

stops.name: Aomori
stops.story: The ferry from Ezo lands you on the windy northern tip of Honshū, among herring sheds and drying nets. Edo is ten stops down the Ōshū road, and every journey starts with one small stall.

stops.name: Sannohe
stops.line: The road climbs into the snowy hills.
stops.story: A quiet hill town under the ruins of an old castle, where the road starts to climb and the snow comes early. Woodcutters and charcoal burners bring you the season's aches.

stops.name: Morioka
stops.line: A castle town of smiths and tools.
stops.story: A castle town of iron kettles and stone bridges, where three rivers meet. The smiths here will sell their tools to any healer with coin.

stops.name: Hanamaki
stops.line: Hot springs and a crowded waiting bench.
stops.story: Steam rises from the hot springs, and the bathhouse bench is full of soaking, grumbling patients. They're in no hurry, but every round they wait makes them harder to please.

stops.name: Ichinoseki
stops.line: A river gorge full of rival healers.
stops.story: Below the gorge, the tea houses send dumplings across the river on ropes. Here you meet healers who mark their patients with an oni and stand guard over them.

stops.name: Sendai
stops.story: The great castle city of the north, rich with merchants and summer lanterns. Well-off patients pay their thanks in gifts.

stops.name: Fukushima
stops.line: A fever sweeps the silk town.
stops.story: A fever has swept through the silk town. Every patient is contagious, and if one is sent home uncured, both healers pay.

stops.name: Shirakawa
stops.line: The barrier gate, and a noble guest.
stops.story: The old barrier gate between north and south, where every traveller shows their papers. A noble guest asks you, quietly, for a cure in two stages.

stops.name: Utsunomiya
stops.line: A river ferry that won't wait.
stops.story: The roads from Nikkō and the north meet here at the river. The ferry won't wait, the bench is short, and your rival keeps their cards hidden.

stops.name: Edo
stops.line: The Shōgun's city, at the end of the road.
stops.story: The end of the road: the Shōgun's city, a million people and the best healers in the land. Your royal patient is the Shōgun himself.

intro.basics: Gentle patients, close to the centre. Learn to brew.
intro.symptoms: Harder patients, some with symptom marks the route must pass through.
intro.bench: The waiting bench: patients who wait need more ingredients but pay more, and the last one goes home each round.
intro.claims: Claims: lay an oni to keep a patient for yourself.
intro.quirks: Quirks: frail, nervous, stubborn and contagious patients.
intro.gifts: Gifts: some patients thank you with mon, cards, an oni or a cheaper tool.
intro.outbreak: Boss: every patient is contagious. If one goes home uncured, both healers lose 2.
intro.royal: Your royal patient: a private cure in two stages, paid in full at the end.
intro.river: A short bench of three spots, and hidden hands.
intro.shogun: Final boss: the Shōgun is your royal patient, and your rival starts ahead.

hard.name: Hardcore
hard.sub: Lose a stop and the journey is over: back to the first town, medicine chest emptied. No retries, no replays.
hard.lost: The journey ends in {place}. Back to the start.
